subject: MERGE statement
notes: Rule: 'The MERGE statement merges all records contained on the files referenced by file-name-2 and file-name-3.' (cite.py --check 14.9.24.4 -> OK §14.9.24.4 1)). Code: EmitMerge emits one SortNextInput + EmitInputFile per USING file (READ loop releasing EVERY record until an unsuccessful read), then CobolSort.Merge sequences the statement's store (SortWork.Sequence -> SequenceMerge): every released record is in its USING stream's slice of the in-memory chunk or, once the chunk has filled the memory limit, on that stream's run file (WriteStreamChunks), and SortMergeCursor.Next returns a record until every run is exhausted, so no record is dropped in memory or spilled (kb/Work PB3339). Probe probe/merge-p2/m1.cob (3 USING files, 4+3+2 records, OUTPUT PROCEDURE): all 9 records returned, CNT=09, identical at --std 2023 and --std 85. Golden 2002/pb993 leg 6 (USING SRC-A {A,C} SRC-B {B,D}) expects L6-OUT=A,B,C,D - all four records of both files, computed from the rule. || editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (MERGE is a COBOL-85 statement; the rule text is unchanged) Past the memory limit: SortWorkBoundTests.AMergeManyTimesTheLimit_KeepsInputFileOrder_WithinTheLimit and SortWorkSpillConformanceTests (60,000 records of two USING files, all returned).
